Fixture: 34_icc_gray_table_32x32_lossless.jxl (+ 34_icc_gray_table_32x32_lossless.icc)
32x32 greyscale, mathematically lossless, greyscale ICC profile with a
512-entry 16-bit tone curve -- the E.4.5 command-4 predictor case

Purpose
-------
Targets slice 4 (18181-1 E.4.5). Same shape as fixture 30 but the kTRC
payload is a 512-entry curveType table (a gamma-2.2 ramp, 16 bits per
entry) instead of a single gamma value, which makes the profile 1356
bytes -- an order of magnitude larger than its tag table.

A smooth 16-bit ramp is exactly what E.4.5's command 4 is for: shuffle
the payload into high-byte and low-byte planes, then run an Nth-order
predictor over 2-byte integers `stride` bytes back. This fixture is the
smallest one here whose decode depends on that predictor being right,
including the carry between the two bytes of each entry.

Provenance
----------
  Encoder:      cjxl v0.13.0 196a43d9 [_AVX2_,SSE4,SSE2] {GNU 15.2.0}
  libjxl rev:   196a43d996aa6ed33ebf98812a7c6d43b2b6d01b (v0.12-snapshot-2-g196a43d9)
  cjxl flags:   -d 0 -e 3 -x icc_pathname=<profile>
  Built by:     tools/setup-oracles.sh (flags recorded in
                tools/oracle-bin/PINNED_REVISIONS.txt)
  Regenerate:   tools/make-icc-fixtures.sh
                That script IS the recipe; it rewrites the profile and the

                oracle installed.

Verification
------------
tools/make-icc-fixtures.sh checks two things on every run, and refuses to
write the fixture if either fails:

  * djxl --orig_icc_out returns a profile byte-identical to the one cjxl was
    given, so the reference really is what the codestream stores;
  * djxl decodes the pixels to a PNM byte-identical to the source, so the
    stream is mathematically lossless.

tests/e2e_icc.rs then asserts that JPXL's own E.4 decoder reproduces the
reference byte for byte, and repeats the comparison against a live djxl when
one is installed.

cjxl is used strictly as a BLACK BOX: it emits conformant streams for JPXL to
parse. libjxl's source is never read. If a rebuild at a different libjxl
revision changes these digests, that is the point of recording them -- do not
silently update them; note the revision change.
